rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Employers must manage workplace risks for pregnant workers and new mothers as part of providing a safe working environment.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: An individual risk assessment is required for a worker who is pregnant, gave birth within the previous six months or is breastfeeding.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Once the worker provides written notification, the employer must complete the individual assessment and make necessary changes.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: The assessment must consider working conditions and processes that could harm the worker or their child.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Gig-economy, agency and temporary workers should receive the same health-and-safety protection when pregnant or a new mother.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: The assessment should be reviewed as pregnancy progresses or when the work, workplace or medical advice changes.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Employers must take account of relevant medical advice, which may require changes to working conditions or hours.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Regular discussion with the worker is important because mobility, reach, coordination and other capabilities can change during pregnancy.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Controls depend on pregnancy stage, health advice, work activity, exposure, hours, workplace conditions and individual needs.

rows.source: HSE pregnant workers and new mothers
rows.verified: Pregnancy and new-mother evidence is person-, stage-, task- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Vehicle exhaust fumes can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract and create a health risk when inhaled.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Exhaust from carbon-fuelled engines can contain carbon monoxide, which is poisonous.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Prolonged exposure to diesel fumes, especially visible blue or black smoke, can contribute to coughing and breathlessness.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Repeated long-term exposure to diesel exhaust emissions may increase lung-cancer risk.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Workplaces where engines run should have effective ventilation rather than relying only on open access doors.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Static-running vehicles should use a tailpipe exhaust-extraction system, particularly in inspection pits or enclosed workshops.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Extracted exhaust should discharge to a safe outdoor location where it will not re-enter the building or expose nearby people.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Catalytic converters should not be treated as making indoor engine running safe, especially during cold or intermittent operation.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Diesel-exhaust risk depends on engine type, maintenance, fuel, load, smoke condition, duration, enclosure and ventilation effectiveness.

rows.source: HSE diesel engine exhaust controls
rows.verified: Diesel-exhaust evidence is engine-, task-, exposure-, location- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level cancer or poisoning probability.
